title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Lula maintains a consistent lead in recent polling ahead of Brazil’s October 4 first-round vote, with Flávio Bolsonaro as the clear right-wing frontrunner in a likely runoff scenario.** Polls from Datafolha, Quaest, Nexus, and others conducted in August show Lula (PT) at 38–42% in the first round and 43–49% in head-to-head runoffs against Flávio (PL), the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio trails in the 28–36% range initially but narrows the gap to within the margin of error in some runoff simulations.

Jair Bolsonaro remains ineligible until 2030 following a 2023 electoral court ruling and faces ongoing legal consequences related to post-2022 events, preventing his candidacy and channeling right-wing support toward his son. Other registered candidates—including Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Romeu Zema—register only low single-digit support, while additional names such as Pablo Marçal face eligibility barriers. The official campaign period began August 16, with free television and radio advertising starting soon after, aligning trader pricing closely with polling aggregates that position Lula as the strongest favorite while leaving room for movement in a closely contested runoff.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains closely contested, with trader pricing reflecting a fragmented field where no candidate has consolidated broad support. Gavin Newsom at 15.0% has seen earlier momentum erode amid scrutiny of his California record, while Jon Ossoff at 14.2% benefits from appeal in competitive terrain as a Georgia senator. Kamala Harris and others trail as the party weighs primary calendar adjustments starting with South Carolina and potential late entrants or endorsements. Developments such as formal candidacies, polling shifts in early states, or legislative outcomes could widen gaps among the top contenders before the 2028 cycle intensifies.
